content:
Hi,

I've opened #40572 as a draft. It adds periodizedBernoulli1 x = Int.fract x - 1/2 (the 1-periodic first Bernoulli function) with the 
global bound |periodizedBernoulli1 x| ≤ 1/2.

Naming question: bernoulliFun and periodizedBernoulli (on UnitAddCircle) are nearby — is the first Bernoulli function better
expressed via one of those, or kept as this standalone Int.fract form?

Any guidance on naming/placement welcome before I build further.

As I wrote in the PR on GitHub, the Lean code was developed with the assistance of AI (Claude Code CLI), so I would particularly appreciate any advice or feedback on the quality.

Thanks
Rob

We also have this formula in the PNT project (currently near the start of Mertens.lean) and an open issue PNT#1367 to upstream it to Mathlib. Is your work independent of this or are you upstreaming the PNT result?
Hi Alastair, thank you for the link. Yes this is meant to upstream the PNT result, but also meant to be useful/comply with any related mathlib standards/goals.

After that guidance I, (with AI assisted development, Claude Code CLI) have implemented what I believe is a much improved PR,  I've made the two requested changes, please see the GitHub.

  • periodizedBernoulli1 is now bernoulliFun 1 (Int.fract x), which connects it to the existing bernoulliFun infrastructure rather than an ad-hoc named expression, without growing this PR's scope. The general periodizedBernoulli n := bernoulliFun n ∘ Int.fract family and the n-order Euler-Maclaurin formula are queued as a follow-up PR.
  • The statement is standardized on Int.floor throughout (the main theorem and the private floor-correction lemma). The Abel-summation step stays Nat-indexed internally, bridged to the Int.floor statement by a small cast helper, so the Nat/Int mixture is gone.

Rob
